title: Understanding Bootstrapping
text: Bootstrapping is a statistical method that involves resampling with replacement from a dataset to estimate the distribution of a statistic. It is often used to estimate the variance or confidence intervals of a sample statistic.

title: Sample Size Consideration
text: When using bootstrapping, the sample size for each resample is typically the same as the original sample size. In this case, each bootstrap sample would consist of $$500$$ trips.

title: Population vs. Sample
text: The original dataset contains all taxi trips in $$2018$$, while the sample from May $$1$$ contains only $$500$$ trips. Bootstrapping focuses on the sample to estimate the variance of the average duration.

title: Bootstrapping Process
text: To perform bootstrapping, you would repeatedly draw samples of $$500$$ trips with replacement from the May $$1$$ sample and calculate the average duration for each resample. Then, compute the variance of these averages.
